senses.definition: (uncountable) The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later, usually at will.
examples: Memory is a facility common to all animals.

quotes.text: And they say goldfish have no memory. I guess their lives are much like mine. And the little plastic castle is a surprise every time.
quotes.reference: 1998, “Little Plastic Castle”, in Little Plastic Castle, performed by Ani DiFranco:

senses.definition: A record of a thing or an event stored and available for later use by an organism.
examples: I have no memory of that event.
My wedding is one of my happiest memories.
Sam and his friends will never forget the happy memories of the field trip to France.

quotes.text: I know I can't hide from my memory / Though day after day I've tried / I keep sayin', she'll be back / But today again I've lied
quotes.reference: 1971, Chi-Lites, “Have You Seen Her”, in (For God's Sake) Give More Power to the People:

senses.definition: (computing) The part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data (RAM) or unalterable executable code or default data (ROM).
examples: This data passes from the CPU to the memory.

quotes.text: My first microcomputer had 12K of memory. When I expanded to a full 64K, I thought I had all the memory I'd ever need. Hah. I know better now.
quotes.reference: 1987 July 27, Jerry Pournelle, “Law of Expanding Memory: Applications Will Also Expand Until RAM Is Full”, in InfoWorld, volume 9, number 30, InfoWorld Media Group Inc, page 46:

senses.definition: The time within which past events can be or are remembered.
(attributive) Of a material, which returns to its original shape when heated.

quotes.text: These weeds are memories of those worser hours.
